verified_claims: Substituting x=f(y) makes both outer quantities equal to f(y), so the middle quantity is equal to them and f(f(y))+y=2f(y).
For d(t)=f(t)-t, the iterate law f^n(t)=t+n d(t) follows by induction, and positivity of every forward iterate forces d(t)>=0.
At x=f(t), the lower squared margin expands to (t-y)^2+4(t+d(t))(d(t)-d(y)), and the upper squared margin expands to (t-y)^2+2(d(y)-d(t))(2y+d(y)+d(t)).
The two sign-dependent bounds combine validly to give |d(y)-d(t)| <= (y-t)^2/(4 min(t,y)); all denominators are positive and all squaring steps are reversible.
Telescoping this quadratic bound over arbitrarily fine partitions of any compact interval [u,v] contained in the positive reals forces d(v)=d(u) without assuming continuity.
The resulting constant displacement is nonnegative, and every f(x)=x+C with C>=0 satisfies the original chain by RMS-AM-GM; equivalently, both squared margins are (x-y-C)^2.
The affine, power-law, and piecewise orbitwise-shift falsification examples are consistent with the proof and are not used as substitutes for it.
summary: The classification f(x)=x+C for C>=0 is proved completely. Independent algebra checks, edge-case analysis, and counterexample searches found no logical gap, hidden regularity assumption, invalid limiting step, or missing boundary case. This remains a model review rather than an official proof certificate.
transfer_assessment: Reusable: an endpoint-locking substitution can turn a two-sided inequality into equality and yield an exact iterate identity.
Reusable: an orbit-invariant displacement together with positivity of all forward iterates can force a global sign constraint.
Reusable: complementary squared margins can yield a quadratic modulus of variation after a sign split.
Reusable: an O(h^2) local difference bound telescoped over O(1/h) subintervals forces constancy without any assumed continuity.
Reusable: verify the converse by exact factorization of both squared margins, here into the same square.
